messages:
mara: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a telemetry-first 'sensorium' for canary/fallback decisions. Goal: richer signals + small evals, but keep runtime policy boundary simple. Thoughts?
kenji: +1 on telemetry-first. main risk = signal explosion and oscillation. propose a normalized score vector: latency_p50,p90,error_rate,quality_delta(k=eval-set),kv_staleness,cost_spike. everything in [0,1].
olivia: For quality_delta we need a micro-eval set (50-200 queries) run in parallel. sliding window + bootstrap CI so tiny blips don't flip the policy. also weight decay on older samples.
sam: Runtime interface idea: router queries policy service with request metadata + condensed signal vector; policy returns {variant, confidence, mode, fallthrough_ttl}. Keep router stateless about long histories. Example response:```json
{"variant":"v2","confidence":0.82,"mode":"soft_fallback","fallthrough_ttl_s":30}```
kenji: Love the JSON shape. Define modes: soft_fallback = weighted traffic shift over N requests; hard_fallback = immediate 100% reroute; graceful_degrade = strip heavy features (longer context, tool calls).
olivia: We also need probe-only mode: keep routing unchanged but run shadow runs to collect full QA and kv-sim metrics. That prevents premature switches.
kenji: On signal aggregation intervals: 1s granularity for short-term (10m window), 1m aggregated for 24h, 1h for 30d. Normalization must account for tenant baseline (per-customer zscore).
mara: How should rollback budgets work? my thought: policy declares a "budget" (max pct traffic per minute that can be moved) + cooldowns. prevents thrashing during noisy telemetry.
sam: Circuit breakers: per-variant counters for consecutive error bursts + a rolling p95 latency multiplier. If breaker trips -> hard_fallback + alert. Keep counters in router for O(1) check.
rollouts-bot: Canary job started by mara: target progression 2% -> 8% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%. Observability hook: embed canary id in traces.
deploy-bot: deploy log: v2 image pushed to registry sha:deadbeef. Instance count 24.
kenji: Operational concerns: kv cache staleness signal can be noisy when keys hot-swap. prefer sampling keyspace and expose staleness percentile. Also watch for cold-start-induced latency spikes on dedicated nodes.
olivia: A/B eval contract: store per-request seed so we can deterministically replay failing queries. keep 30-day retention of seeds for repro.
mara: Interface boundary decision: policy service gets aggregates + small feature bag (tenant, route, time_of_day, recent_errors). Router keeps short-lived counters and executes immediate breakers. Policy is authoritative for planned rollouts and can push soft weights.
kenji: Security note: signals may contain PII (user prompt length, token counts). strip or hash anything user-facing before sending to policy. keep policy in-mem only, no logs of raw prompts.
sam: Perf note: policy calls must be <5ms median to avoid adding tail to request path. if heavy, call async and use last-known-decision with TTL.
mara: Action items: kenji -> draft API + normalization funcs; olivia -> prototype micro-eval runner + seed store; sam -> router stub for breaker counters + TTL cache. I'll collate and draft updated RFC. :thumbsup:
